story_type: moon lander's own cameras film its engine plume blasting lunar dust during touchdown
hook: Cameras under a lander, filming its engine hit the Moon.
narration: Cameras under a lander, filming its rocket engine blast the surface of the Moon.
This is Firefly's Blue Ghost, coming down in March 2025 with ten NASA instruments aboard.
Four NASA cameras snapped eight pictures a second as it dropped from about twenty six meters.
With no air on the Moon, exhaust throws the dust outward at high speed.
[short pause] Below three meters, the dust swallowed the view.
outcome: Blue Ghost landed successfully near Mons Latreille, in the Moon's Mare Crisium basin.
title: Moon lander films its own touchdown
description:
NASA's SCALPSS cameras on Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost Mission 1 filmed the final descent as the engine plume hit the lunar surface. Blue Ghost landed on March 2, 2025, near Mons Latreille in Mare Crisium.

Footage: NASA video (SCALPSS 1.1 cameras), via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/Final_Out_CRF35

question_comment: Would you trust a robot to land you on the Moon by itself?

extra_sources.excerpt: Firefly Aerospace’s Blue Ghost Mission 1, carrying 10 NASA science and technology instruments, successfully landed at 3:34 a.m. EST on Mar. 2, near a volcanic feature called Mons Latreille within Mare Crisium, a more than 300-mile-wide basin located in the northeast quadrant of the Moon’s near side.

facts.source_quote: a preliminary sequence of the Blue Ghost final descent and landing that NASA researchers stitched together from SCALPSS 1.1’s four short-focal-length cameras, which were capturing photos at 8 frames per second.
